about.title: Newman Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Newman's economy leans heavily on agriculture, food processing, and the small businesses that support them, which means workplace injuries here often involve heavy equipment, repetitive strain, or vehicle-related incidents while on the clock. Under California law, workers' compensation is typically the only path against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim worth exploring. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured workers in Newman with an independent attorney who can review the details of your situation, explain your options in plain terms, and help you understand whether a third-party claim applies alongside any workers' comp benefits you're already pursuing. There's no cost to get that conversation started.

items.title: We Help You See the Full Picture
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it doesn't rule out a claim against a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker. An independent attorney can help sort out which paths actually apply to your situation.

items.title: We Know the Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Getting matched with an attorney early can help make sure nothing gets missed.

items.title: We Understand Retaliation Fears Are Real
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report injuries or file claims. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your protections before you decide what to do.

items.question: I was hurt on a farm job outside Newman — can I still file a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: In most cases, yes. California workers' compensation generally covers agricultural workers just as it does other employees, and it applies regardless of who was at fault for the accident. An independent attorney can review your specific work arrangement to confirm how the law applies to you.

items.question: What if a piece of equipment or a subcontractor caused my injury, not my employer?
items.answer: That's exactly the kind of situation where a third-party claim might come into play alongside workers' comp. If a manufacturer, subcontractor, or another company's negligence contributed to your injury, you may be able to pursue a separate claim with its own 2-year deadline. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney to look into it.

items.question: Do I need to worry about losing my job if I report an injury in Newman?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for employers to retaliate against workers for reporting an on-the-job injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you're concerned about how your employer might react, an independent attorney can walk you through your protections before you take any next steps.
